items.text: Morgan Stanley states that deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.
items.quote: Deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that its deferred cash-based and stock-based compensation programs for current and former employees, including financial advisors in Wealth Management, generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions.
items.quote: The Firm sponsors a number of deferred cash-based compensation programs and stock-based compensation programs for current and former employees, including financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment, which generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that Wealth Management advisor compensation includes a formulaic (production/revenue-based) payout, as higher compensation expense was driven by 'an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors on higher revenues.'
items.quote: primarily due to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors on higher revenues

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that compensation and benefits expenses (firmwide) include base salaries and fixed allowances, formulaic programs, discretionary incentive compensation, amortization of deferred cash and equity awards, changes in fair value of referenced notional DCP investments, carried interest, severance costs and other items such as health and welfare benefits.
items.quote: Compensation and benefits expenses include base salaries and fixed allowances, formulaic programs, discretionary incentive compensation, amortization of deferred cash and equity awards, changes in the fair value of the referenced notional DCP investments, carried interest allocated to employees, severance costs, and other items such as health and welfare benefits.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that in the first quarter of 2026 the Firm reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management advisors.
items.quote: in the first quarter of 2026, the Firm reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management advisors.

items.text: According to trade press reporting, Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, and is not introducing retention bonuses as part of its 2027 pay plans for advisors.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

items.text: According to trade press reporting, Morgan Stanley is not introducing retention bonuses as part of its 2027 pay plans for advisors, adhering to a more traditional approach.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses as part of their 2027 pay plans for advisors, adhering to a more traditional approach.
